scope: 50 exact historical relationship rows; full old claim, endpoint scopes and author mapping inspected. Exact repeated endpoint text reused after its first inspection; no inference from matching labels/pages.

rows.review_disposition: The minister/deputy bar is an internal design mechanism of 1C628 (123–124). Preserve its three-year exclusion as printed here, separately from Robespierre’s later four-year rule on 150. No self-edge is necessary after that explicit repair.

Page 155 supports the conservative secondary-elector qualification within the completed settlement. Internalization requires the main parent to state the apparent silver-mark concession and the less visible wealth restriction.

Page 133 explicitly connects bank distrust and John Law’s memory with Mirabeau’s successful land-bond alternative. Internalize that causal choice in 5193, rather than dropping it behind the general phrase land-backed origins.

The tricolour’s composition and militia origin belong within 2056. Preserve Parisian red/blue joined to Bourbon white as a named symbolic route, not a general assertion that every later use of the flag is explained by the Guard.

Page 143 says the armed southern counter-revolution galvanized the clubs. This is substantive mobilization, not taxonomy. Retire an extra edge only with that specific response preserved in ABA54 and Jalès access through 888503; generic religious controversy or émigré labels alone do not suffice.
Pages 133–134 directly support the Extraordinary Fund and land security for initial bonds. These are components of 5193, with the original bond versus later currency distinction explicit.

The oath’s continuing commitment is renewed during defiance (105–106). EE3 preserves opposition but should explicitly state renewal of the oath as the basis of continuing constituent authority; avoid a mechanical single-cause account.

The reverse consequence formulation concerns the same supported oath-to-defiance sequence. The final EE3 rationale and 1E3F/1DB77 parent sequence must preserve the renewal, not merely an abstract contrast.

Religious disputes stimulated club foundation and mobilization (142). The current ABA54 stance preserves the causal stimulus; retain its specific press/polarization evidence and correct the retirement reason from nonspecific association to explicit parent retention.

Page 126 explains distrust of noble-led regular troops and dependence on the Guard. Internalize this contrast in 2056’s meaning; unreliability is not synonymous with universal desertion or total inability to use the army.

Pages 125–126 distinguish courts, local administrators and the Guard as coercive instrument, with no dedicated police provision. Internalization requires those institutional roles in 2056, not only a public-order label.

Lafayette commands the Guard yet cannot assume its obedience (148,154). The extra commands edge can retire with the explicit command/dependence dilemma in 5784/2056; do not erase its refusal at Saint-Cloud.
Varennes compounded the breakdown of consensus (151–153). 2C2C9 preserves a contributing effect rather than making the flight the cause of earlier religious polarization.
Varennes precedes and intensifies intervention expectations. 9EBFC correctly reverses the malformed normalized direction; use direct pages 152/156–157 rather than domestic amendments on 155.

The Guard joins popular mobilization and coercive restraint under martial law. This tension can be internalized in 2056 if both roles, the red flag and municipal authority to order fire are explicit; no generic popular-intervention dossier should be copied wholesale.

Contacts with religious unrest are real but do not establish émigré control of the west. Retire the vague linked_to edge with named southern contacts in 7593 and distinct western localism in 60DA/FB2D; do not use 146–147 southern evidence as if it directly describes Vendéan organization.

The amnesty failed to stop emigration (156). Reversed 88C9 only says withdrawal weakened the settlement and does not by itself retain failed conciliation. Add the amnesty’s failure explicitly to 1C628/8A61 and the edge rationale or precise internalized mapping.

Pages 139/143 describe defeated Nîmes Catholics redirecting the Jalès federation. The authored AC7C relationship already links C455 to 888503 using 300. Rebind this old causal requirement there with 143/300 support rather than claiming C455 alone internalizes the separate Jalès target.

Page 105 supports court alteration of the programme. Preserve queen/Artois participation and the distinction between policy modification and the broader constitutional rupture in 1DB77; a generic whole-event cause edge may retire.
The reverse British-model contrast is supported on 120/123–124. As for row 51, 1DBAA needs rejected and accepted proposals distinguished explicitly.

Pages 154–155 directly support suppression enabling final amendments. 894D preserves the direction and qualified effect; this is temporary freedom from popular pressure, not lasting national agreement.
Page 146 supports Mirabeau’s rejection of aristocratic restoration. 55CBD preserves the contrast with Artois’s plans without labelling Mirabeau a counter-revolutionary.

The suspensive veto is a concrete element of executive design (123). 1DBAA preserves that relation provided final rationale states the compromise, and 1C628 retains the veto’s duration and legislative limitation.
Page 156 links army weakness to perceived foreign danger. CFF220 correctly reverses made_dangerous_by and avoids asserting that emigration caused the diplomatic declaration.

The manifesto left behind is evidence of royal repudiation (151–152), not identical to the motivation relation 325384. Preserve its evidentiary role explicitly inside 621651 and 44E68; change the crosswalk to partial/internalized retention rather than claiming motivates alone is equivalent.
Pages 133–134 support the fund’s use of nationalized Church assets. Reversing uses to C242→5193 secures preserves the actual financial dependency without promising currency stability.

The broad related link between multi-year popular intervention and Versailles spectators adds no precise claim beyond the concrete crowd/Assembly routes. Retire it while retaining the specific episodes in 4304 and related event parents.
Church lands provide the financial basis for initial assignats (133–134). 468E preserves the basis_for direction and should remain distinguished from the later success or failure of paper currency.

Barnave opposed free-coloured concessions, not slavery preservation (151). 456AF repairs the wrong target; retain his pro-colonial-order stance in parent 530 and do not imply he advocated emancipation.

Compensation enlarged public debt (132) and drove supplementary paper issues (134). This is a substantive mechanism. Retire the extra worsens edge only with that connection explicitly in 5193 and the financial crisis parent; later E4C3 officeholder losses are a different consequence.
The oath crisis reinforces the king’s doubts, explicitly on 147. 388ABB’s schism facet preserves the relation; old pages 142/144/145 supply policy context but are not the best causal passage.
Montauban is a local instance of confessional power struggle (138). Internalization in C455 is coherent once its inventories, opposing militia and victims remain distinct from Nîmes.

Necker’s threatened resignation intensifies immediate crowd pressure after the Royal Session (106–107); it does not cause the whole 1788–1790 concept. Preserve that event sequence in 1DB77/4304 and qualify the broad old cause accordingly.
The manifesto makes later constitutional acceptance suspect (152,157–158). EC492 preserves that direction and the distinction between formal acceptance and credibility.
Religious/political alienation helps motivate escape. 325384 correctly reverses caused_by; its repaired direct page set includes omitted 147 and removes unrelated labour/geographical pages.
War rumours sustained polarization despite Feuillant conciliation (156–157). CE048 retains that effect with diplomatic intention and French reception separated.

Defeated Nîmes leaders feed Jalès mobilization, but page 138 alone is not that sequence. Rebind to AC7C and 888503 using 143/300 rather than retire as nonspecific; 7593 preserves émigré coordination only as another aspect.

The constituent mission contrasts with royal supremacy. F8C9’s effect on royal authority is not the same relation. Rebind this contrast to expanded EE3 and its 1E3F/1DB77 endpoints, using 105–106 for the mission and opposition.

The ministerial separation arose partly from rejecting Mirabeau’s British-style proposal (123–124), not merely the veto decision. Expand 1DBAA’s rationale to rejected parliamentary executive links and preserve the three-year bar in 1C628.
Amnesty accompanies promulgation (156–157), an internal event within 1C628. Preserve both timing and the limited success of attempted reconciliation; no separate accompanies edge is required.

The Assembly’s sovereignty declaration prompted the royal intervention (105–106). EE3’s opposition alone is not a causal statement. Retain the response-to-17-June sequence in 1DB77 main meaning and the revised rationale, without claiming the oath preceded all planning.
The Royal Session’s asserted supremacy conflicts with the constituent oath (105–106). EE3 faithfully preserves this contrast with reversed endpoints; it is not an inversion of causal chronology.

Page 153 supports nationwide Guard/vigilance/refractory persecution and Jacobin mobilization. F20FE covers the club facet only. Preserve the wider emergency inside 621651, not silently narrow the entire old composite to clubs.

Locked-hall preparations belong to the Royal Session sequence (105–106). Opposes alone does not retain a part_of/sequence claim. Bind the explicit preparations in 1DB77 and locked-hall-to-oath sequence in 1E3F; correct the historical mapping accordingly.

Pages 146–147 establish early exile plans, while 156/302 show later mass officer expansion. Retire the vague expands_into edge with precise early/later stages in 7593/8A61; FA919’s later elite outcomes do not prove the 1791 expansion.

Full pages 87–88 re-read: jubilation after Necker’s return led to attacks, troop firing and concern over uncontrollable effervescence. The specific episode survives 2B7B; a generic example_of the multi-year popular-intervention dossier can retire without treating all projected targets as its content.

F8C9 preserves June defiance contributing to royal-strategy collapse, with the explicit qualification that enforceable authority collapsed after July. Retain that chronology; 106–108 alone do not describe the Bastille outcome.

The entire later equality dossier is not part of early third-estate unity. Retire the misleading part_of formulation, preserving the actual shared civil/fiscal aims in AD1724 and later limits in separate subjects.
Pages 154–155 support repression enabling completion. 894D correctly reverses the malformed normalized enabled_by relation; do not treat the constitution as causing the earlier massacre.
Page 146 supports Mirabeau’s constitutional royalism contrasted with émigré restoration. 55CBD retains the exact distinction; similarity of escape schemes does not negate divergent aims.
